title: Projective completion of a finite rank vector bundle
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal E$ a locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of constant rank $d\geq0$, with vector bundle $\pi:E=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\to S$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. The relative Proj
$$\overline E=\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_S\oplus\mathcal E)$$
[def-nagata-relative-proj, lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] is Noetherian, and its structural morphism $r:\overline E\to S$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $t$ is the degree-one section induced by $1$ in the first summand, there is a canonical open immersion $j:E\xrightarrow{\sim}D_+(t)\hookrightarrow\overline E$ with $rj=\pi$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. On every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ trivializing $\mathcal E$, this is the chart $D_+(t)\subset\mathbf P^d_V=\operatorname{Proj}R[t,x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ given on coordinate rings by $x_i\mapsto x_i/t$ [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. These identifications commute with restriction and changes of linear frame. The morphism $\pi$ is separated and finite type, and $E$ is Noetherian [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Thus $(j,r)$ is a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. At $d=0$ it is the identity compactification of $S$.

source.place: Tag 01OA (section-projective-bundle); relative Proj and standard charts, with properness of projective space. Agent-written global chart gluing: returned proof step 2.

proof.text: Put $F=\mathcal O_S\oplus\mathcal E$. A frame of $\mathcal E$ gives a frame $(1,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$ of $F$, so $F$ is locally free of rank $d+1$, hence quasi-coherent by [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Its symmetric algebra is quasi-coherent and its sections over an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ are $\operatorname{Sym}_R(F(V))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. Use the symmetric grading of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]; restrictions preserve it because they send each degree-one generator to its restriction and preserve products. Therefore [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] constructs $r:\overline E=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(F)\to S$. On a trivializing affine $V$, [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] identifies its graded algebra with $R[t,x_1,\ldots,x_d]$: each generator has degree one, so the algebra identification preserves degrees. The graded equivalence induces the Proj identification by [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality](2), giving $r^{-1}(V)=\mathbf P^d_V$. The affine restriction identifications commute with further restriction by [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists].

source.place: Tag 01OA (section-projective-bundle), Tag 01OB (definition-projective-bundle), Tag 01OE (lemma-projective-space-bundle); symmetric algebra grading and local polynomial description

proof.text: On a trivializing affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] identifies $E|_V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]$. The standard-chart interface of [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] identifies $D_+(t)$ in the local model of Step 1 with $\operatorname{Spec}C_{(t),0}$, where $C=R[t,x_1,\ldots,x_d]$. Explicitly the $R$-algebra map $\alpha:R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\to C_{(t),0}$ sends $y_i$ to $x_i/t$. Define its inverse on a homogeneous fraction by $f(t,x)/t^m\mapsto f(1,y)$ for $f$ homogeneous of degree $m$, using [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. This is well-defined: a localization relation $t^k(t^nf-t^mg)=0$ becomes $f(1,y)=g(1,y)$ on setting $t=1$. It respects sums and products, and $f(t,x)/t^m=f(1,x/t)$ shows the two composites are identities. The inverse of $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ gives $E|_V\cong D_+(t)$, followed by its open inclusion. These maps are over $V$ because $\alpha$ fixes $R$.

source.place: Tag 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), explicit dehomogenization on the relative-Proj standard chart; no comparison with base-change projective space is invoked

proof.text: Check agreement of these chart identifications. On an affine refinement of the overlap of two trivializing opens, write $e'_j=\sum_i g_{ij}e_i$ with $G$ invertible. The summand $\mathcal O_S$ is fixed, so $t'=t$, and the symmetric-algebra generator maps give $x'_j=\sum_i g_{ij}x_i$. This is the same frame change as the vector-bundle coordinates $y'_j=\sum_i g_{ij}y_i$ in [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Consequently $x'_j/t=\sum_i g_{ij}(x_i/t)$, so the two chart maps agree on each polynomial generator and on the base ring, hence agree. Their inverses agree too. Restriction to a smaller affine open simply restricts the coefficients in these equalities: the relative Proj restriction maps in [def-nagata-relative-proj] are the degree-zero homogeneous localization maps. Thus the opens $D_+(t)$ agree on overlaps and define an open $U\subseteq\overline E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to glue the local maps $E|_V\to U$ and their inverses $U|_V\to E$. Their composites and their structural maps agree locally, so uniqueness in the same lemma gives inverse global isomorphisms $E\cong U$ and $rj=\pi$. This defines the canonical open immersion $j$ and proves restriction and frame compatibility. Intersections of affine opens have only been covered by affine refinements, never assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 01OA (section-projective-bundle) and section-relative-proj-via-glueing; explicit agent-written generator calculation for chart compatibility

proof.text: Put $F=\mathcal O_S\oplus\mathcal E$ as in Step 1. It is locally free of rank $d+1$. Apply [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry] with $B=S$, $n=d$ and this $F$. Its properness assertion is for the actual relative Proj $\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}F$, exactly the $r:\overline E\to S$ constructed in Step 1, so $r$ is proper. Proper includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since the assumed base $S$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] then makes $\overline E$ Noetherian. No identification with the separately defined base-change projective space is needed.

Through the isomorphism $E\cong U$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] to the open $U\subseteq\overline E$ to obtain that $E$ is Noetherian. For every affine open $W\subseteq\overline E$, its preimage under $j$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $E$, so the same lemma makes it quasi-compact. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact and [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] gives that $j$ is finite type. Both $j$ and $r$ are finite type, so [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) makes $\pi=rj$ finite type. The diagonal of $\pi$ is the base change of the closed immersion $\Delta_r:\overline E\to\overline E\times_S\overline E$ to $E\times_SE$: its inverse image is the diagonal copy of $E$, since $j$ identifies $E$ with the open subscheme $U$. Base change of a closed immersion is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Hence $\Delta_\pi$ is closed and $\pi$ is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

The factorization $\pi=rj$ with $j$ open and $r$ proper is a compactification by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], using $S$ itself as the auxiliary base; $E$ and $S$ are finite type over that base by Step 5 and the identity map respectively. When $d=0$, the local homogeneous ring is $R[t]$ and its irrelevant ideal is $(t)$. Thus every point of $\operatorname{Proj}R[t]$ lies in $D_+(t)$, and the chart from Step 2 has coordinate ring $R$ with structural map the identity. Likewise the rank-zero vector-bundle pieces have coordinate ring $R$. The local identities glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], so $E=\overline E=S$ under their canonical identifications and both $j$ and $r$ are identities. This includes the empty base and the zero ring.
